card.statement: Select MegaMoE GEMM tile configurations using layer/rank routing distributions at fixed SM allocation, retaining a fixed-tactic fallback.
card.mechanism: Pinned DeepGEMM chooses block_m from uniform expected tokens per expert plus sqrt margin. At fixed token count, real histograms can change the number of expert tiles and padding; changing legal block_m may trade weight reloads against padded arithmetic. Preserve expert IDs/weights, placement, quantization, communication policy and SM allocation.
card.proposed_change: First qualify a small per-layer and token-bucket tactic table from actual physical histogram evidence; use a fixed tactic within each captured layer/bucket where stable. Only if within-bucket variation matters, consider GPU-resident histogram-conditioned selection. Expose legal block_m through DeepGEMM API/layout rather than assume existing FlashInfer environment flag reaches MegaMoE. Co-design symmetric buffer, scale layout, ring divisibility and rank compatibility before any dynamic launch. No implementation authorized.

supportsources.quote: the best fused-MoE kernel changes with routing skew and token count
Expected tokens per expert, plus a one-sigma routing margin

counterevidence: DA-MoE source measurements use TRTLLM/FlashInfer NVFP4 on DeepSeek-V3/Kimi, not Flash-1017 MXFP4 MegaMoE. Source full MoE-graph measurements are not request E2E measurements.

Paper reports ~14us full selector/control overhead per graph; a faster tactic can lose overall. PR5194 newer PrimsTS experiments show many near-neutral or slower cells; no advantage over best fixed tactic established.

DeepGEMM381 only calibrated EP8/E256/K8/H7168/I2048 and near128expectedTPE; changed wave size saved~1.27% in one testedcell, broader policies regressed. Target EP4/E384/K6 differs; do not import its flag or gain.
Routing histogram is not sufficient latency estimator; locality, communication, activation shape, quantization and synchronization still matter.
